# Localization and extremal-body route

## A precise continuity lemma for an admissible finite-fiber class

Let Z be a fixed finite subset of Z^n. For each z in Z let K_z and K_{j,z}
be nonempty compact convex bodies in R^d, with d>=1, and suppose
K_{j,z} -> K_z in Hausdorff distance. Put
S=union_z ({z} x K_z), S_j=union_z ({z} x K_{j,z}), and normalize the sums
of fiber Lebesgue measures to probability measures mu and mu_j. Then

  max_{y in S_j} depth_{mu_j}(y) -> max_{y in S} depth_mu(y).

This statement does not require that the unions be induced by a convex body.

Proof. All the fibers lie in a fixed ball B_R in R^d. Hausdorff convergence
to a full-dimensional compact convex body implies convergence of its
indicator function almost everywhere: points in the interior eventually
belong, points outside eventually do not, and its boundary has Lebesgue
measure zero. Dominated convergence gives L1 convergence. Summing over the
finite index set and normalizing therefore gives total variation convergence
of mu_j to mu.

For any point p in the full ambient space, define its depth by the usual
infimum over closed halfspaces containing p, whether or not p belongs to the
measure's support. The uniform inequality

  |depth_{mu_j}(p)-depth_mu(p)| <= ||mu_j-mu||_TV

follows by taking the infimum after the uniform bound on every halfspace.

It remains to control continuous displacement of p within a fixed integer
fiber. For p=(z,x), p'=(z,x'), translate any closed halfspace containing p by
(0,x'-x), obtaining a closed halfspace containing p'. If the continuous
normal component is zero, its intersection with every integer fiber is
unchanged. Otherwise, within every fiber its bounding hyperplane moves by
Euclidean distance at most |x'-x|. The change of fiber volume is at most
omega_{d-1} R^{d-1}|x'-x|, because orthogonal projection of any fiber onto
the normal's orthogonal complement lies in B_R^{d-1}. Consequently

  |depth_mu(z,x)-depth_mu(z,x')|
    <= |Z| omega_{d-1} R^{d-1}|x-x'| / sum_z vol_d(K_z).

(The convention omega_0=1 applies when d=1.) This argument is uniform over
all ambient halfspaces, including arbitrarily oblique ones and ones whose
boundaries contain whole integer fibers.

Each fiber is compact, and the displayed Lipschitz bound gives existence of
its maximum depth; a finite maximum gives existence over S. For a maximizing
point in S_j, choose a point in the corresponding K_z within the Hausdorff
distance, and apply the Lipschitz and total variation bounds. This yields
the upper bound on the limit superior. Transfer a fixed maximizing point of
S to the corresponding K_{j,z} for the reverse inequality. QED.

This lemma justifies minimizers in a compact, fixed-index, nondegenerate
family of fibers. It does not supply such a normalization for all convex
bodies. In particular, ordinary Hausdorff convergence of the ambient bodies
does not imply the hypothesis about the integer fibers.

## Why ordinary body convergence is insufficient

In n=d=1 let C_j=[1/j,1+1/j] x [0,1] for j>=2. The induced set has just the
integer fiber z=1, so its maximum normalized halfspace depth is 1/2.
The Hausdorff limit C=[0,1] x [0,1] has the two fibers z=0,1 and maximum
normalized depth 1/4. Thus the maximized-depth functional is not continuous
under Hausdorff convergence of ambient convex bodies. The fiber at z=0
appears with positive measure only in the limit. Any extremal-body argument
must track this phenomenon explicitly.

## Exact invariance under the admissible affine shadow motions

For any U in GL_n(Z), integer a, real matrix B of size d by n, invertible
real matrix A of size d by d, and vector b in R^d, the map

  T(z,x)=(Uz+a, Ax+Bz+b)

preserves Z^n x R^d, maps ambient closed halfspaces bijectively to ambient
closed halfspaces, and multiplies every full-dimensional fiber volume by
|det A|. Therefore its normalized depth functional is exactly invariant.
In particular, the shadow motion x -> x+t Bz produces no improvement of
maximized depth; any useful deformation must depart from this affine class
and needs a genuinely new monotonicity argument.

## Status of the mechanism

The proved continuity lemma can support a variational argument only after a
compact class with stable integer fibers and positive limiting fiber volumes
has been justified. No monotone non-affine shadow deformation has been proved.
Standard one-needle localization does not automatically preserve the finite
family of strict small-cap inequalities needed to exclude every mixed-integer
center; merely invoking localization at that point would leave a theorem-
strength gap.

## Uniform densification lemma, with a complete measure argument

Fix r>=1 and d>=0, and put D=r+d. Let L_j be full-rank lattices in R^r
having fundamental parallelepipeds F_j of diameter rho_j -> 0 and covolume
c_j. Arbitrary affine translates of L_j are allowed. Let K_j be convex bodies
in R^D converging in Hausdorff distance to a full-dimensional convex body K.
On K_j intersect ((a_j+L_j) x R^d), let mu_j be mixed volume normalized to
mass one. Let mu be normalized D-dimensional Lebesgue measure on K. Then

  sup_{ambient closed halfspaces H} |mu_j(H)-mu(H)| -> 0,

and the maxima of halfspace depth over their respective supports converge.
In particular, this applies to d=0 and counts the sampled lattice points.

Proof of the measure assertion. Choose a fixed ball B_R containing all K_j.
For a compact convex E subset B_R, tile R^r by z+F_j with z in a_j+L_j,
choosing the fundamental cell so its distance from z is at most rho_j.
Define the measurable step set

  T_j(E)=union_z ((z+F_j) x E_z).

Cell boundary overlaps have zero D-dimensional measure, and Fubini gives
vol_D(T_j(E))=c_j sum_z vol_d(E_z), including the d=0 convention. Moreover

  E_{-rho_j} subset T_j(E) subset E+rho_j B_D,

where E_{-rho} is the Euclidean inner parallel set. The first inclusion
holds because rounding the first r coordinates to their cell's lattice point
moves a point by at most rho_j; the second follows by the reverse move.

The volume of the annulus (E+rho B_D) minus E_{-rho} tends to zero uniformly
among compact convex E subset B_R as rho -> 0. Here is a compactness proof
that includes arbitrarily thin E. Otherwise take E_j and rho_j -> 0 with
annulus volume bounded below. Blaschke selection gives a Hausdorff limit E.
If E has empty interior, E_j+rho_j B_D converges to a zero-volume convex set,
so its volume tends to zero, a contradiction. If E has interior, Hausdorff
convergence of convex bodies implies inner and outer parallel volumes both
converge to vol_D(E), again a contradiction. The same conclusion holds for
empty E. This proves a uniform error tending to zero between the sampled
mixed volume times c_j and vol_D(E).

Apply this to every E=K_j intersect H. Separately,
|vol_D(K_j intersect H)-vol_D(K intersect H)| is bounded uniformly in H by
the L1 distance between 1_{K_j} and 1_K, which tends to zero. Applying the
same estimates to the total masses and normalizing proves the assertion for
all closed halfspaces; no boundary-null assumption is imposed on mu_j.

For the depth assertion, halfspace probabilities being uniformly close
implies the corresponding pointwise depth functions are uniformly close on
the entire ambient space. The depth function for mu is uniformly Lipschitz
in the location of its point: translating a halfspace by a vector h changes
its K-volume by at most omega_{D-1} R^{D-1}|h|. Every point of K can be
approximated by points of the sampled K_j: first approximate it by an interior
point of K, then round only its first r coordinates, then let that interior
approximation approach the original point. Conversely, points of K_j have
limit points only in K. These facts and compactness give convergence of the
maxima. QED.

The same proof works with an additional fixed finite set of residual integer
fibers, provided those residual fibers converge to full-dimensional bodies
in the r+d continuous coordinates and no positive-volume residual fiber
appears or disappears. Apply the uniform sampling bound to each residual
fiber and sum; move candidate points within a fixed residual integer fiber.

## Boundary collapse gives unequal limiting weights

Let C be the unit disk in R^2, and let a>0 be fixed. For small epsilon>0,
take an affine lattice in its first coordinate with consecutive elements
-1+epsilon and 1-a epsilon; its spacing is 2-(a+1)epsilon. These are the only
lattice coordinates intersecting C. The corresponding fiber lengths are

  2 sqrt(2 epsilon-epsilon^2),
  2 sqrt(2 a epsilon-a^2 epsilon^2).

Their ratio tends to 1:sqrt(a). The affine lattices converge locally to the
lattice containing -1 and 1, and the limit intersection with C consists of
the two tangent points. Its intrinsic H_0 gives equal weights to those
points, whereas the normalized mixed measures tend to weights
1/(1+sqrt(a)) and sqrt(a)/(1+sqrt(a)). Thus a classification of limiting
closed subgroups alone does not identify the limiting normalized measure.

## Densification constant audit

Replacing r integer dimensions by continuous dimensions changes the target
from 2^{-n} gamma_d to 2^{-(n-r)} gamma_{d+r}. The latter is strictly larger
when d>=1, r>=1, and when d=0, r>=2. There is equality when d=0, r=1:
2 gamma_1=gamma_0=1. Any induction using strict slack must exclude or separately
handle that equality case.

## Removing tiny fibers can increase the global optimal depth

The exact four-dimensional simplex construction in candidate 8dd62757ee4f1859 also
rules out a natural localization monotonicity. Let T be a 4-simplex, let v
be one of its vertices, and let B_r=v+r(T-v). Define

  C_r=conv(({-1} x B_r) union ({0} x T) union ({1} x B_r)).

At r=1/10 the rational barycentric-cap certificate proves that every point
of the middle fiber has normalized depth strictly below

  gamma_4 (1+r^4)/(1+2r^4) < gamma_4.

Every point of either endpoint fiber also has depth at most
r^4/[2(1+2r^4)], by a halfspace isolating that endpoint fiber and taking a
continuous cap of at most half its volume. Therefore the global maximized
depth of C_{1/10} is strictly below gamma_4.

At r=0, both endpoint fibers are singletons carrying zero H_4 measure, and
the entire normalized measure is uniform on the middle simplex T. Its
centroid has depth gamma_4, while no point has greater depth. Thus shrinking
the two small fibers all the way to zero increases the maximized depth.
The family C_r remains full-dimensional for every r>=0. Consequently,
removing low-mass fibers by this convex homothetic deformation is not a
valid depth-nonincreasing reduction toward a simpler extremal body.
